title: Closing a Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency Agreement
content:
**Patient accounts settlement standard — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.**

**The rule.** An agreement is closed only when its account balance and its deposit balance are both zero. A converted agreement stays open while any private charge, credit or deposit remains on it. A cancelled admission refunds any advance payment and deposit in full, because no day was charged.

**Read from the system record before closing:** the agreement's account balance (what the resident owes; a negative figure is a credit balance) and its deposit balance.

| Account balance | Deposit balance | May the agreement close? |
|---|---|---|
| Zero | Zero | Yes |
| Zero | Above zero | No |
| Owed or in credit | Zero | No |

**Which agreements close this way.** A discharged agreement closes once the final statement is settled, the deposit disposed of and any credit refunded; a converted agreement closes once no private balance or deposit is left on it. A planned admission that does not take place is cancelled, and every advance payment and deposit on it is refunded in full.
